edinburgh_maryking_guide.text: Welcome to Mary King's Close. Watch your head. The ceilings are older than the building above them.
A close is a narrow lane between tall tenements, and this one is named for a 17th-century resident, Mary King.
When the Royal Exchange, now the City Chambers, was built in the 1750s, the upper floors were taken down and the lower streets were built over. It opened to visitors in 2003.

edinburgh_maryking_historian.text: The ghost stories are mostly modern. The real people here were ordinary Edinburgh families, packed in tight, with the best view of a very steep street.
